newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says will cut up to 800 jobs at Parsons.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says will cut up to 800 jobs at Parsons.

text.p: Aero-engines and industrial power group Rolls-Royce Plc said on Friday it intended to cut 400 jobs early in the new year at the Parsons Power Generation subsidiary which it is trying to sell.
It also warned another 400 from the 1,700 workforce might have to go depending on how current sales negotiations progress.
But a spokesman said several prospective buyers were now examining the business and it was hoped a deal could be clinched before April next year.
"There could be a further 400 (jobs to go) but we hope very much to avoid that," said Peter Barnes-Wallis.
But the first 400 jobs had to go because the workload was declining. "We are not chasing large orders," he said.
"We cannot afford to keep a workforce of this size when we have so much extra capacity," he added.
Rolls put its Parsons and International Combustion units up for sale in July when it said it wanted to exit the large steam power generation business, if not by sale then by closure.
Barnes-Wallis said the costs of the job losses would be covered by the 240 million stg of provisions which were made for the disposals in the half-year results.
International Combustion has also attracted some buying interest but negotiations were not so far advanced, he said.
"The process is slightly behind because we gave priority to selling Parsons. But there are a number of prospective buyers taking a look," he said.
